current.text: He is back at full health and projected to start for Indiana with Haliburton, Nembhard, Siakam and Zubac.
Kelly Oubre Jr. joined Indiana and is projected as the sixth man. If Oubre starts, he would take Nesmith's spot.
Without Haliburton last season, his overall FG% fell from 51 to 41 percent. His FG% at the rim fell from 67 to 39 and on twos from 59 to 46.
Experts expect his FG% to bounce back with Haliburton back, because he will not have to create his own shot. One speaker is very confident he improves.
If his shooting gets back to 48 to 50 percent, he could be a top 100 player.

One expert ranks him in the 110 to 130 range and calls him the late-round swing on this team, without feeling great about it. He would not take him in 10 or 12 team leagues, only as a 10th player in 14 team leagues.
Expected line is about 30 minutes, 13 points and a couple of threes per game.
He should be worth more in category leagues than in points leagues this season.
Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21 and has 15 back-to-backs this season.
The 3-4-3 playoff schedule is not ideal for a season that ends March 28.
Coach Rick Carlisle keeps regular-season minutes low, even for healthy players, and rests players on back-to-backs.
Lloyd expects Carlisle to manage Haliburton's minutes early in the season.

durable.text: He is a great three-point shooter.
He is not a self-creator. His efficiency depends on a playmaker like Haliburton setting him up.
He is a high-foul wing, and his defensive stats are poor for his minutes.
His assists are weak for his position, so he suits punt AST builds.
